pages.name: Ultrasonic pipe thickness testing
pages.context: API 570 and API 574 (t-min, CMLs, corrosion rate inputs), ASME B31.3 and B31.1, ASME Section V Article 23 (SE-797), ASTM E797; straight-beam dual-element gauges, step-block calibration, high-temperature readings, readings through coating only where the gauge mode is verified, CML grids, data for the owner engineer/AI who computes remaining life.

pages.name: Ultrasonic weld inspection
pages.context: Manual angle-beam (shear wave) UT of groove welds: AWS D1.1 Clause 8 Part F and AWS D1.5 for bridges, ASME Section V Article 4, ASME B31.3 para 344.6, API 1104. ASME Section VIII allows UT in place of RT only under conditions (Code Case 2235 / Appendix 12) that need computerized imaging techniques Atlantis does not offer on these pages, so say that plainly. Reference levels, scanning patterns, sizing limits, coverage.

pages.name: Ultrasonic boiler tube thickness testing
pages.context: Thickness surveys of waterwall, superheater, reheater and economizer tubes and HRSG tubes during outages; ASME Section I, NBIC Part 2, state boiler inspectors, EPRI boiler tube failure guidance; fireside erosion, sootblower erosion, corrosion fatigue context; grid layouts, scaffold and access, surface prep of tubes, high-temperature not applicable during outage; recovery boiler floor and wall tubes in pulp mills under BLRBAC practices (composite tubes need specialist techniques, not ours). Oxide scale measurement is a specialist technique, not offered here.

pages.name: Ultrasonic testing of castings and forgings
pages.context: ASTM A388 / ASME SA-388 (heavy steel forgings), ASTM A609 / SA-609 (carbon and low-alloy steel castings), ASTM E114, ASME Section V Article 23; straight-beam and angle-beam scanning, back-reflection and flat-bottom-hole references, attenuation and coarse grain in castings, quality levels set by the purchase order; shop and foundry work, receiving inspection, shafts and rings.

pages.name: Magnetic particle weld inspection
pages.context: ASME Section V Article 7, ASTM E709, AWS D1.1 Clause 8, ASME B31.3 para 344.3, API 1104; AC and DC yokes, lifting power checks, prods (arc strike risk), field direction and two perpendicular magnetizations, wet fluorescent vs visible dry powder, pie gauge / field indicators, lighting and black light intensity, demagnetization when required; root, hot pass and final weld checks; cracks at toes; undercut is VT.

pages.name: Magnetic particle inspection of lifting equipment
pages.context: Crane hooks, shackles, eye bolts, padeyes and lifting lugs, spreader bars and below-the-hook devices, crane sheaves and pins; ASME B30.10 (hooks), B30.26 (rigging hardware), B30.20 (below-the-hook lifting devices), ASME BTH-1; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.179 (overhead cranes), 1910.184 (slings), 1926 Subpart CC; NDT is set by the owner program, the manufacturer or a qualified person (the standards call for periodic inspection; do not claim they always mandate MT); throat opening and wear are visual measurements; Atlantis reports indications, the owner or qualified person decides removal from service.

pages.name: Magnetic particle inspection of castings and forgings
pages.context: ASTM E1444 and E709, ASTM A275 / ASME SA-275 (MT of steel forgings), MSS SP-53 (MT of steel castings and forgings for valves, flanges and fittings), ASTM E125 reference photographs for casting indications, ASME Section V Article 7; bench units vs portable yokes for field and receiving inspection, head shot and coil shot concepts for parts, residual vs continuous method; valve bodies, flanges, shafts, gears, hooks.

pages.name: Magnetic particle inspection of structural steel and bridges
pages.context: AWS D1.1 for buildings and structures, AWS D1.5 for bridges (state DOT specifications), FHWA National Bridge Inspection Standards (23 CFR 650 Subpart C) and fracture-critical members, AISC 360 Chapter N quality control and quality assurance roles; field MT on fillet and groove welds, coped beams, connection plates, crane runway girders; the special inspector or the engineer of record decides acceptance on building work, and Atlantis does not offer IBC special inspection agency services.

pages.name: Dye penetrant weld inspection
pages.context: ASME Section V Article 6, ASTM E165 (field) and E1417 (process), AWS D1.1 Clause 8, ASME B31.3 para 344.4, API 1104; stainless, aluminum and nickel alloy welds where MT cannot be used; solvent-removable visible dye in the field, fluorescent where specified; temperature range and qualification outside it (Article 6 standard range 40–125 °F / 5–52 °C), dwell times, removal, developer, interpretation and bleed-out, root pass and back-gouge checks.

pages.name: Penetrant testing of stainless steel and nickel alloys
pages.context: Austenitic stainless, duplex, nickel alloys and titanium; ASME Section V Article 6 contaminant limits (sulfur and halogens) for penetrant materials used on these alloys; ASME BPE hygienic systems; chloride stress corrosion cracking; post-cleaning so residues do not stay in product contact surfaces; cryogenic and high-purity service; MT not possible on austenitic grades.

pages.name: Penetrant testing of castings
pages.context: ASTM E165 and E1417, MSS SP-93 (liquid penetrant examination of castings and forgings for valves, flanges and fittings), ASTM E433 reference photographs, ASME Section V Article 6 for code castings; aluminum, stainless and nonferrous castings; as-cast surface roughness and background, water-washable vs solvent-removable systems, porosity vs shrinkage vs cracks, rework and re-examination after grinding.
